note: Election of the whole of Belfast Corporation (an alderman and three councillors in each of the 15 wards) under the Elections and Franchise Act (Northern Ireland) 1946, polled Wednesday 18 September 1946; the first since the war. Seven wards were counted on the morning of 19 September and the rest that afternoon; the Unionists kept an overall majority of 26 (Belfast Telegraph, 19 and 20 September 1946). Falls, Smithfield and Windsor had no councillors' poll and Court, Smithfield and Windsor no aldermanic poll (Belfast News-Letter, 5 September 1946). Poll 58.2 per cent.
correctionNote: Corrected from the Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3): Robert Hill's vote is 4,090 as the register records it (previously 4,000, from the newspaper source). Checked on the page image of the Northern Whig, 20 September 1946, p. 1 (w8-review, Nov 2026): the Whig prints the same figures as the Belfast Telegraph, R. Hill 4,000 placed third below W. B. Brown's 4,059, with electorate 14,454, poll 8,418, 701 spoiled and a majority of 464 (Morgan over Thompson, the retiring Independent Unionist: not the ward's elected-over-defeated margin, so not recorded as one); the poll is recorded. Hill's 4,090 from the register is kept pending a re-check of the register entry, although both papers' order of declaration fits 4,000.
